title: Surge-aware version locking and fallback matrix for canary rollouts
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Goal: implement a surge-aware session locking and fallback matrix that preserves rollout safety (canary/A-B) while preventing capacity storms from permanently trapping traffic on canary variants. Problem: existing session pin semantics + strict pin TTLs lead to either sticky canaries (bad under pressure) or excessive user-flapping when TTLs are too short. This ticket designs and implements a middle-ground: deterministic version locking with adaptive escape under surge, a prioritized fallback matrix of compatible variants, and control knobs for region/tier-aware relaxation during capacity pressure.
acceptance_criteria: 1) New routing policy can be enabled via a feature flag and defaulted off for all customers
2) Under simulated surge (2x request rate for 5m) the policy reduces canary-induced queue growth by >= 40% without exceeding 2x baseline 99th latency for stable variant
3) Session locks respect configured TTLs but allow probabilistic escape when per-queue pressure crosses thresholds
4) Fallback matrix respects model compatibility (tokenization/architecture) and prefers lower-cost quantized variants when latency budget is close
5) End-to-end e2e tests cover: normal rollouts, surge-induced escapes, geo-failover where primary region is starved
6) Dashboard shows per-model variant traffic split, escape events, and capacity-triggered relaxations
implementation_notes: Design overview: maintain per-session "version_lock" metadata (model_version, locked_at, ttl, escape_score). On each request, router evaluates queue_utilization and cpu/gpu_saturation heuristics to compute an escape_probability.

Escape policy: base_escape = max(0, (util - util_target) / (util_max - util_target)). final_escape_prob = clamp(base_escape * surge_multiplier * (1 - sticky_coef), 0, 1). If random() < final_escape_prob -> allowversion_relaxation.

Prioritized fallback matrix: for each model_version compute ordered list [same-arch-quantized, same-arch-full, compatible-llm-lite, fallback-stable]. Each entry annotated with expected latency multiplier and quality degradation estimate.

Region/tier aware: when region capacity < regional_threshold, increase surge_multiplier for requests from that region so local lockdown is relaxed earlier; for premium tiers reduce surge_multiplier to favor stickiness.

Operational knobs: pin_ttl (default 30m), sticky_coef (0..1), util_target (0.6), util_max (0.95), regional_threshold (0.75), burst_window_seconds (300). All overload thresholds configurable per-customer.
Backward compatibility: feature flag runtime to toggle between old and new behavior; maintain session metadata compatibility with legacy orchestrator until migration completes.

Data retention: emit escape event log including session_id, previous_version, new_version, reason_code, queue_metrics, and model_variant_ranking. Logs persisted 30d by default for debugging and evals.

rollback_criteria: Escape events exceed 0.5% of total requests for a canary and correlate with >10% quality regression alerts
Regional latency 99th increases >25% for stable variant during enabled window
Unrecoverable traffic shift where >90% of session locks migrated off-stable variant
Feature flag rollback path tested and <5min rollback to previous behavior
monitoring_playbook: Create Grafana alerts for: escape_rate > 0.2% sustained 5m, variant_traffic_ratio deviation > 15% vs expected, region_utilization > regional_threshold
On alert: enable verbose escape logging, route to SRE runbook, optionally throttle canary traffic via circuit breaker
Post-incident: capture session traces, analyze escape decisions and timeline, and create retrospective note in incident tracker
